highlights: CVE-2026-77158: Double free of disks array in qemuAgentGetDisks
qemu: Add poll-weight support for iothreads
CVE-2026-18917: Integer overflow in RPC handler for virNodeGetFreePages
Arm: Significant cleanup of the vgic-v5 PPI support which was merged in 7.1. This makes the code more maintainable, and squashes a couple of bugs in the meantime.
Arm: Set of fixes for the handling of the MMU in an NV context, particularly VNCR-triggered faults. S1POE support is fixed as well.
Arm: Large set of pKVM fixes, mostly addressing recurring issues around hypervisor tracking of donated pages in obscure cases where the donation could fail and leave things in a bizarre state.
vhost-host-user support for offloading real-time clock handling from the hypervisor when using virtio-rtc
ARM: support for new architectural CPU features (too many to list here, see full changelog)
ARM: support for new imx8mp-evk machine type (based on i.MX 8MM Evaluation kit)
qemu: Add preserve-running action for <on_crash>
bhyve: implement virDomainRename()
build: Add option to control building libvirtd
qemu: Add support for standalone VNC server
qemu: Record selected virtio video device model into the XML
bhyve: Extend the guest agent support

Arm: Add support for tracing in the standalone EL2 hypervisor code, which should help both debugging and performance analysis.  This uses the new infrastructure for 'remote' trace buffers that can be exposed by non-kernel entities such as firmware, and which came through the tracing tree.
Arm: Add support for GICv5 Per Processor Interrupts (PPIs), as the starting point for supporting the new GIC architecture in KVM.

Arm: Finally add support for pKVM protected guests, where pages are unmapped from the host as they are faulted into the guest and can be shared back from the guest using pKVM hypercalls.  Protected guests are created using a new machine type identifier.  As the elusive guestmem has not yet delivered on its promises, anonymous memory is also supported.

virtio-gpu support for native context drivers and specifying a unique resolution for each output.

Loongarch: Fix return value for memory reads from and writes to in-kernel devices.
ARM: Add support for FEAT_IDST, allowing ID registers that are not implemented to be reported as a normal trap rather than as an UNDEF exception.
ARM: Add sanitisation of the VTCR_EL2 register, fixing a number of UXN/PXN/XN bugs in the process.

guest_memfd: Add support for host userspace mapping of guest_memfd-backed memory for VM types that do NOT use support KVM_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTE_PRIVATE (which isn't precisely the same thing as CoCo VMs, since x86's SEV-MEM and SEV-ES have no way to detect private vs. shared).
ARM: Add support for FF-A 1.2 as the secure memory conduit for pKVM, allowing more registers to be used as part of the message payload.
ARM: Change the way pKVM allocates its VM handles, making sure that the privileged hypervisor is never tricked into using uninitialised data.

ARM: Userspace control of the 'nASSGIcap' GICv3 feature, allowing userspace to disable support for SGIs w/o an active state on hardware that previously advertised it unconditionally.

Generic: New ioctl KVM_SET_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES allowing userspace to specify per-page attributes for a given page of guest memory; right now the only attribute is whether the guest expects to access memory via guest_memfd or not, which in Confidential SVMs backed by SEV-SNP, TDX or ARM64 pKVM is checked by firmware or hypervisor that guarantees confidentiality (AMD PSP, Intel TDX module, or EL2 in the case of pKVM).

ARM: Provide a virtual cache topology to the guest to avoid inconsistencies with migration on heterogenous systems. Non secure software has no practical need to traverse the caches by set/way in the first place.

ARM: Add support for taking stage-2 access faults in parallel. This was an accidental omission in the original parallel faults implementation, but should provide a marginal improvement to machines w/o FEAT_HAFDBS (such as hardware from the fruit company).

a large rewrite of MMU emulation.  KVM MIPS can now use MMU notifiers to support copy-on-write, KSM, idle page tracking, swapping, ballooning and everything else.  KVM_CAP_READONLY_MEM is also supported, so that writes to some memory regions can be treated as MMIO.  The new MMU also paves the way for hardware virtualization support.
some refactoring of nested VMX entry/exit code, preparing for live migration support of nested hypervisors

Introduce NVDIMM memory model

Switching of MSR_TSC_AUX in SVM was thought to cause a host misbehavior, but it was later cleared of those doubts and the patch moved code to a hot path, so we reverted it.  That patch also needed a fix for 32 bit builds and both were reverted in one go.
Al Viro noticed that a fix for a leak in an error path was not valid with the given API and provided a better fix, so the original patch was reverted.
x86: miscellaneous fixes, AVIC support (local APIC virtualization, AMD version)

s390: polling for interrupts after a VCPU goes to halted state is now enabled for s390; use hardware provided information about facility bits that do not need any hypervisor activity, and other fixes for cpu models and facilities; improve perf output; floating interrupt controller improvements.

support for VT-d posted interrupts (i.e. PCI devices can inject interrupts directly into vCPUs).  This introduces a new component (in virt/lib/) that connects VFIO and KVM together.  The same infrastructure will be used for ARM interrupt forwarding as well.
a number of fixes for the arch-timer
introducing proper level-triggered semantics for the arch-timers
ARM: several features are in progress but missed the 4.2 deadline. So here is just a smattering of bug fixes, plus enabling the VFIO integration.
Common code: Support for multiple address spaces; for now it is used only for x86 SMM but the s390 folks also have plans.
s390: Some fixes/refactorings/optimizations, plus support for 2GB pages.
ARM, PPC, s390 all had only small fixes
For x86: small performance improvements (though only on weird guests)
For x86: usual round of hardware-compliancy fixes from Nadav
a lot of s390 changes: optimizations, support for migration, GDB support and more
ARM changes are pretty small: support for the PSCI 0.2 hypercall interface on both the guest and the host (the latter acked by Catalin)

for x86, a larger set of changes is scheduled for 3.17.  Still, we have a few emulator bugfixes and support for running nested fully-virtualized Xen guests (para-virtualized Xen guests have always worked).  And some optimizations too.
